messages:
Andrew: Heads up — a customer on Android SDK v1.4.2 reporting short 429 spikes during their hourly batch sync. They have burst cushion showing >50 tokens but still see ~10s of 429s. Repro steps and logs below.

Sam: Account ID? Can you paste a minimal repro?

Andrew: acct: acct-8291. Repro steps: 1) start sync where client sends 30 parallel generate calls (small prompts) over HTTP/2 connection, 2) each request ~120 tokens, 3) spikes last ~8-12s then clear. Happens every hour during backfill job start.

Andrew: Logs:
```
2026-02-14T14:00:03Z INFO request id=xyz route=/v1/generate status=200 tokens=118
2026-02-14T14:00:05Z INFO request id=abc route=/v1/generate status=429 error=rate_limited x-burst-remaining=0 x-burst-window-ms=60000
2026-02-14T14:00:06Z INFO request id=def route=/v1/generate status=200 tokens=121
```

Maya: Interesting — SDK uses HTTP/2 multiplexing right? That pattern (many concurrent streams on one connection) can create a very tight microburst at the server side. Burst cushion is per-account but smoothing + concurrent in-flight streams can exhaust the cushion faster than the dashboard sampling shows.

Sam: @Maya can you confirm whether the token-level cushion is decremented immediately on accept or smoothed across the window? Customer says dashboard showed cushion >50 when they started.

Maya: Short answer: cushion accounting is based on a sliding window; we decrement as requests start but smoothing logic applies a recovery over the window. If 30 simultaneous starts hit, the instantaneous remaining can reach 0 even if rolling-average still >0 in UI sampling. UI refresh rate can be misleading here.

Andrew: Ah, makes sense. The customer is surprised because their dashboard looked fine right before job. They batch-opened 30 streams from a single device.

Sam: Workarounds to give them now: 1) reduce parallelism to <=6 concurrently, 2) add randomized jitter to start times across the batch, or 3) use short exponential backoff on 429 with small jitter to spread retries. Could also move to dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.

Andrew: I can ask them to try parallelism=6 and report. Any SDK changes we can recommend?

Maya: On infra side we'll add a quick telemetry check for microburst clustering and confirm whether per-route concurrency gates interacted with smoothing to produce temporary 429s. Long term we can improve UI sampling and surface "instant depletion" warnings.

Sam: I'll create a ticket and attach the logs. Temporary mitigation instructions to customer and ask for a follow-up in 24h.

SupportBot: Ticket S-45212 created and assigned to infra. ETA: triage within 4h.

Andrew: Customer tried reduce-to-6 — immediate fix, no 429s in next two runs.

Maya: Good — filed infra bug INF-1187 to evaluate smoothing math when many in-flight streams arrive within same ms.

Sam: Closing loop with customer and marking as "mitigated". We'll update once INF-1187 has analysis. :thumbsup:
